newsitem.title: USA: Go all out on disclosure, MSRB chair warns issuers.
newsitem.headline: Go all out on disclosure, MSRB chair warns issuers.

text.p: MSRB Chairman Roger Hayes urged tax-exempt bond issuers to go all out on disclosure because the Securities and Exchange Commission is watching.

"My personal feeling is anything you feel is pertinent, even just useful, ought to be disclosed for your own protection," said Hayes, who took the helm of the 15-member Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board this fall.

Hayes said the SEC has a limited arsenal of weapons that it can use against municipal issuers, but it is an effective one. He compared SEC strategy to the nabbing of gangster Al Capone by such federal enforcement agencies as the Internal Revenue Service.
"They got Al Capone for tax evasion," Hayes said. "In some of the enforcement cases (in the muni arena, the SEC) has gone after issuers not for failure to disclose, but fraud.
"Disclosure has to be one of your protections," said Hayes, managing director of NationsBanc Capital Markets, Inc.
Hayes added that he is not suggesting that municipalities are crooks.

The SEC in November 1994 approved amendments to its muni disclosure Rule 15c2-12. The amendments bar dealers from underwriting municipal bonds unless the issuer has pledged to provide information about its finances and about newsbreaking events for the life of the bonds.
